newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan produces 13,000 bpd, hopes to reach 43,000.
newsitem.headline: Sudan produces 13,000 bpd, hopes to reach 43,000.

text.p: Sudanese oil production has reached 13,000 barrels per day (bpd) and is expected to reach 43,000 bpd by the end of next year, the official news agency SUNA said on Wednesday.

Energy and Mining Minister Awad Ahmed al-Jaz told parliament on Tuesday that production at the Heglig field in the southwest was expected to increase from 5,000 bpd to 10,000 bpd by the end of the year and to 25,000 bpd next May, SUNA reported.
But al-Jaz said at the inaugural ceremony of the field in June that eight wells there were already producing 10,000 bpd.
Oil production at the Adar Yiel field, also in southern Sudan, which currently averages 1,300 bpd, is expected to reach up to 10,000 bpd by the end of 1997.
SUNA did not say where the balance of 6,700 bpd of current production was coming from.

Al-Jaz said experimental production at the Wahda field in the south, where rebels have been fighting government troops since 1983, would begin next April at an initial rate of 3,000 bpd, rising to 5,000 bpd in July 1997.
The Sharif and Abu Gabra fields in the southwest will produce up to 3,000 bpd by the end of this year, he added.
Sudan imports oil worth about $360 million a year.
